sources.title: Argentine and international historical accounts of the 1943 military coup, the 1946 election, the 1955 overthrow, the 18-year exile (1955-1973), and the 1973 return to power

persistence.rationale: Sustained political relevance and eventually returned to the presidency after 18 years in exile across five different countries — an extraordinarily long, well-documented persistence, not a brief absence.

adaptability.rationale: Adapted to residing in five different host countries (Paraguay, Panama, Venezuela, the Dominican Republic, Spain) over 18 years while sustaining his political movement remotely, then successfully re-entered Argentine politics via democratic election in 1973.

leadership_drive.rationale: Built and sustained a political movement (Peronism/Justicialism) that remained the dominant force in Argentine politics even while officially banned and its founder in exile for nearly two decades.

planning_orientation.rationale: Systematically built a labor and union political base during his tenure as Labor Secretary (1943-1945), before ever holding the presidency — a documented, deliberate base-building strategy.

persuasiveness.rationale: Sustained massive documented popular support across nearly three decades, including through his party's official ban and his own 18-year absence from the country — a remarkable, well-documented persuasive durability.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained pursuit of political power and legacy across an unusually long career, returning to and winning the presidency again at age 78.

impact_motivation.rationale: Sustained ideological commitment to Justicialism and labor rights across decades, including during exile when there was no immediate personal power benefit to maintaining the movement, inferred from that sustained commitment.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained direct conflict with the Argentine military and political establishment across decades — the 1955 coup that removed him, sustained opposition during exile, and continued tension after his 1973 return.

proactive_agency.rationale: Personally organized his own return from exile and re-entry into Argentine politics after nearly two decades away, a self-directed undertaking rather than one arranged by others.

collaboration.rationale: Sustained a well-documented political partnership with Eva Perón, whose own independent political activity in the labor ministry and on women's suffrage substantially amplified the movement's reach — a genuine, sustained collaborative partnership, not a figurehead relationship.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Rose through military ranks to the rank of General, a documented career credential preceding his political career.

ambiguity_tolerance.rationale: Sustained political relevance through 18 years of uncertain, shifting exile circumstances across five different countries, inferred from that documented sustained relevance despite the uncertainty.

independent_thinking.rationale: Developed Justicialism as a documented, deliberately distinct "third way" ideology positioned as neither capitalist nor communist, a specific ideological departure from the era's dominant Cold War frameworks.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Sustained direct public leadership and confrontation with political rivals across his career, inferred from the documented pattern of his public political conduct.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Returned to Argentina in 1973 despite ongoing political violence, documented by the fact that a massacre occurred at the airport rally welcoming him back — a real, foreseeable danger he returned into.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Functioned as a career military officer, a labor minister, and a president — a documented range of roles, though the depth of evidence outside the political domain specifically is thinner, hence inference-level.

autonomy_need.rationale: Maintained an independent "Justicialist" ideological path distinct from both Cold War blocs, inferred from the sustained, consistent positioning of the movement he founded.

provenance.notes: Roster-13 new-intake batch (2026-09): Latin America pick. The 18-year exile and 1973 return is treated as the strongest single piece of evidence, corroborated across independent Argentine and international historical accounts, not a single tradition. His documented press-restriction and political-prisoner record during his rule is a real, known gap in this evidence pack's coverage — not reaching the same instance-level specificity as the exile/return material — rather than an oversight. Scored to completion before any eligibility check was run.
